Rashi on Pesachim 42a:10:1.english: Not in the sun - Because the heat of the sun warms [the dough].

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:10:2.hebrew: ולא בחמי חמה - במים שהוחמו בחמה, וכ"ש בחמי האור:
Rashi on Pesachim 42a:10:2.english: Nor with [water] heated by the sun - With water that was heated in the sun, and all the more so with [water] heated by fire.

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:10:3.hebrew: הגרופים מן המולייר - דוד גדול של נחושת, ותלוי על האור כל שעה, ונחושתו עבה, ואפי' כשאין שם אור, מים שבשוליו חמים או פושרין:
Rashi on Pesachim 42a:10:3.english: [Water] scooped from the mulyar - A large copper cauldron that hangs over the fire at all times, and its copper is thick; and even when there is no fire there, the water at its bottom is hot or lukewarm.

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:10:4.hebrew: גרופים - לשון שיריים, שממצין מנחושתו של שוליו:
Rashi on Pesachim 42a:10:4.english: Collected [gerufim] - An expression [denoting] remnants, which are drained from the copper of its bottom.

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:10:5.hebrew: ואל תגביה ידה מן התנור - כלומר, תהא עוסקת בבצק כל שעה:
Rashi on Pesachim 42a:10:5.english: And she should not lift her hand from the oven - That is to say, she should be occupied with the dough at all times.

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:10:6.english: With which she coats - She smears the surface of the loaf with water.

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:10:7.english: In which she cools her hands - For that [water] with which she smooths [the dough] becomes warm from the heat of her hands and the dough.

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:11:1.english: She transgressed and kneaded - With warm water.

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:12:1.hebrew: לא נתבקעו מותרות - ואע"ג דתנא אין לותתין, הכא נמי ל"ש, הואיל ואנו רואין שלא החמיץ, שאין שם לא סימני שיאור ולא סימני סידוק:
Rashi on Pesachim 42a:12:1.english: [If] they did not split, they are permitted - Even though [the baraita] taught "one may not soak," here too there is no difference, since we see that it did not become leavened, for there are neither signs of si'ur [incipient leavening] nor signs of cracking.

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:13:1.hebrew: מחיתא מחיתינהו - כולם אריגה אחת אריגת'. משום דבחדא איסורא דרבנן תנא "אם עבר מותר באכילה", בעית למימר נמי בכולהו:
Rashi on Pesachim 42a:13:1.english: [Are they] woven [in the same] weaving - All of them, their weaving is one weaving. Because regarding one rabbinic prohibition [the Tanna] taught, "If one transgressed, it is permitted for consumption," do you want to say [the same] regarding all of them as well?

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:13:2.hebrew: היכא דאתמר - בהדיא דלא קנסינן ליה, אתמר; והיכא דלא אתמר, לא אתמר. והלכך, עברה ולשה בחמין, קרובה למזיד היתה ואסור, ולא דמי לבציקות של נכרים דאמרינן (לעיל דף מ.) ממלא אדם כריסו מהן, דהכא בעינן למיקנסה דעברה אדרבנן. מעשה אורג מתרגמינן עובד מחי (שמות כ״ח:ל״ב):
Rashi on Pesachim 42a:13:2.english: Where it was stated - [Where] it was explicitly stated that we do not penalize him, it was stated; and where it was not stated, it was not stated. Therefore, [if] she transgressed and kneaded [dough] with warm water, she was close to [acting] intentionally and [the dough] is prohibited; and it is not comparable to the doughs of gentiles, regarding which we say (above, 40a) [that] a person may fill his stomach with them, for here we wish to penalize her because she transgressed a rabbinic [enactment]. "The work of a weaver" [is] translated [into Aramaic as] oved mechi (Exodus 28:32).

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:15:1.hebrew: ואלו עוברין - עליהן בבל יראה ובבל ימצא. וכולהו מפרש להו בגמרא: זיתום, וזומן, וקולן, ועמילן:
Rashi on Pesachim 42a:15:1.english: And these [one] transgresses - [the prohibitions of] "it shall not be seen" and "it shall not be found" on account of them. And all of them are explained in the Gemara: zitom, zoman, kolan, and amilan.

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:16:1.english: Women’s adornments - In the Gemara it explains [what these are].

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:17:1.hebrew: מין דגן - חמשה מינין: חיטין, ושעורין, וכוסמין, ושבולת שועל, ושיפון:
Rashi on Pesachim 42a:17:1.english: A type of grain - Five species: wheat, barley, spelt, oats, and rye.

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:17:2.hebrew: ואין בהן כרת - אם אכלן, אבל לאו יש באכילתן, ובגמרא יליף לה כולה:
Rashi on Pesachim 42a:17:2.english: And there is no karet in them - If one ate them; however, there is a negative prohibition in eating them, and in the Gemara it derives all of it.

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:18:1.english: Blocks - [This is] an expression of stopping up.

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:19:1.hebrew: מסמא את העינים משום מילחא - מלח סדומית יש שמסמא את העינים, כשנוגע במלח וחוזר ונוגע בעין:
Rashi on Pesachim 42a:19:1.english: It blinds the eyes due to the salt - There is Sodomite salt that blinds the eyes when [one] touches the salt and then touches the eye.

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:19:3.hebrew: קומניתא דאומא - עיפושא, פת שמתעפש לאחר זמן בתוך הכותח:
Rashi on Pesachim 42a:19:3.english: Mold of bread - Moldiness, [referring to] bread that becomes moldy after some time in the kutach.

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:1:1.english: It is Rabbi Yehuda - Who holds [that] a prohibition derived by implication from a positive statement is a prohibition.

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:1:2.hebrew: שרוע - הוא שאחת מעיניו גדולה ואחת קטנה, וכן שאר אברים:
Rashi on Pesachim 42a:1:2.english: Too long [sarua] - This is [an animal] that has one of its eyes large and one small, and likewise [with] other limbs.

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:1:3.english: Kalut - [An animal] whose hooves are unsplit [fused].

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:1:4.hebrew: נדבה תעשה אותו - לדמיו הקדישהו לבדק הבית, ולנדר להעלות קרבן לא ירצה. וכתב "אותו": אותו בעל מום אתה מתפיס לקדושת בדק הבית, ואין אתה מתפיס תמימים הראויין למזבח לבדק הבית:
Rashi on Pesachim 42a:1:4.english: You may offer it as a free-will offering - For its value you may consecrate it for maintaining the Temple, "but for a vow" — to offer [it as] a sacrifice — "it shall not be accepted." And [Scripture] wrote "it": it, a blemished [animal], you may consecrate with the sanctity of Temple maintenance, but you may not consecrate unblemished [animals] that are fit for the altar for maintaining the Temple.

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:20:1.english: And bend [one's] stature - That is to say, they weaken his strength.

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:20:2.hebrew: ירק חי - כגון כרישין ובצלים וחזרין, כשאוכל מהן הרבה תמיד:
Rashi on Pesachim 42a:20:2.english: Raw vegetables - Such as leeks, onions, and lettuce, when one eats a lot of them regularly.

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:2:1.english: And the Lord spoke, etc. - It is written at the beginning of the portion.

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:4:1.english: No is stated with regard to [these] matters - [This is] a notarikon of leimor (“saying”).

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:5:1.hebrew: לאו אמור - אמור להן שיש איסור לאו בדברים, והכא גבי פסח נמי כתיב בתחלת הפרשה "ויאמר ה' אל משה ואל אהרן לאמר":
Rashi on Pesachim 42a:5:1.english: Say a prohibition [lav emor] - Say to them that there is a negative prohibition in [these] matters, and here, regarding the Paschal offering as well, it is written at the beginning of the section, "And the Lord spoke to Moses and to Aaron [in the land of Egypt], saying" [Exodus 12:1].

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:6:1.hebrew: האישבורן - לשון שבירה, שמשתבר הקרקע ויש בקעים שהמים נאספים ושוהין בתוכן, ואין נבלעין ומחמיצין:
Rashi on Pesachim 42a:6:1.english: Where [the water] collects [ha'ishboren] - [It is] an expression of breaking [shevirah], where the ground is broken and there are fissures in which the water gathers and remains, and is not absorbed, and [thus] becomes leavened.

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:7:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן: הא דנפישי דקוו, הא דלא נפישי דלא קוו - כשהן מרובות, הן נקוות אל מקום אחד ואין נבלעות מהר ומחמיצות; וכשהן מועטות, לא קוו:
Rashi on Pesachim 42a:7:1.english: This is our reading: This [case is] where there is much, so that it collects; that [case is] where there is not much, so that it does not collect - When there is much [water], it collects in one place and is not absorbed quickly, and it leavens; and when there is little, it does not collect.

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:8:1.hebrew: שלנו - בלילה, מפני שבימי ניסן המעיינות חמין, שעדיין ימות הגשמים הן, כדאמרינן במי שהיה (לקמן פסחים צד:): בימות הגשמים חמה מהלכת בשיפולו של רקיע, לפיכך כל העולם צונן ומעיינות חמין. הלכך, מלינן בלילה ומצטננין:
Rashi on Pesachim 42a:8:1.english: [Water] that rested - Overnight, because in the days of Nisan the springs are warm, since it is still the rainy season, as we say in [the chapter] Mi Shehayah (later, Pesachim 94b): During the rainy season, the sun travels in the lower part of the firmament; therefore, the entire world is cold and the springs are warm. Therefore, one leaves them overnight and they cool down.

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:9:1.hebrew: דרשה רב מתנה - ובלשון הקודש היו דורשין, וכסבורין השומעין שמים שלו הוא אומר:
Rashi on Pesachim 42a:9:1.english: Rav Matnah expounded it - And they would expound in the Holy Tongue [Hebrew], and the listeners thought that he was saying his [own] water.

Rashi on Pesachim 42a:9:2.english: Devitu - [This is] the Aramaic translation of lanu [that rested overnight] (devitu).

Tosafot on Pesachim 42a:15:1.hebrew: ואלו עוברין בפסח - פ"ה: לעבור עליהן בבל יראה ובבל ימצא. וגם ריב"א מדקדק מלשון "עוברים", דמשמע עוברין מן העולם. ואין נראה לר"ת, דמשמע דכל הנך מרבינן מ"כל מחמצת לא תאכלו", ואפילו באכילה לא הוה מיחייב אי לאו דרבייא קרא, ומהיכי תיתי בל יראה ובל ימצא? ונראה לר"ת, ד"אלו עוברין" פי' האוכלין, ו"עוברין" היינו מעל השולחן, דלאו בני מיכל נינהו, אבל בל יראה ליכא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 42a:15:1.english: "And these pass [overin] on Passover" - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: [It means] to transgress through them [the prohibitions of] "it shall not be seen" and "it shall not be found." And Riva also infers [this] from the wording "overin," which implies passing away from the world. But this does not appear [correct] to Rabbeinu Tam, because it is implied that all these are included from [the verse] "you shall eat nothing leavened," and one would not even be liable for eating [them] had the verse not included [them] — so from where would we derive [the prohibitions of] "it shall not be seen" and "it shall not be found"? Rather, it appears to Rabbeinu Tam that "these overin" refers to the foods [themselves], and "overin" means [they are removed] from upon the table, as they are not fit for eating — but there is no [prohibition of] "it shall not be seen."

Tosafot on Pesachim 42a:16:1.hebrew: רבי אליעזר אומר אף תכשיטי נשים - היינו חמץ נוקשה, ואפילו הוי חמץ דגן גמור על ידי תערובות, מ"מ מדקאמר "אף" משמע דמודה לת"ק, ובגמרא אמרי' דרבי אליעזר סבר נוקשה בעיניה בלא כלום. לכך נראה דגרס "רבי אלעזר" בחד מינייהו, או במתני' או בגמרא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 42a:16:1.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: Also women's adornments - This refers to chametz nuksheh [hardened, inferior leaven], and even if it is complete grain chametz [present] through a mixture, nevertheless, since he says "also," it implies that he agrees with the first Tanna [regarding the other items in the Mishnah]. Yet in the Gemara we say that Rabbi Eliezer holds that nuksheh by itself is nothing [i.e., carries no prohibition at all]. Therefore, it appears that [the text] should read "Rabbi Elazar" in one of them — either in the Mishnah or in the Gemara.

Tosafot on Pesachim 42a:4:1.hebrew: לאמר לימד על כל הפרשה שהיא בלאו - נראה לר"י דהיינו דוקא בהנך דברים דאית בהו לאו הבא מכלל עשה, אבל שאר דברים לא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 42a:4:1.english: "Leimor [saying] teaches regarding the entire passage that it is [subject to] a negative prohibition" - It appears to the Ri that this [applies] specifically to those matters in which there is a negative prohibition derived from a positive commandment, but [to] other matters, no.
